correctness.rationale: Schwarz subordination reduces the universal radius to containment of phi(D_r) in the parabolic UCV domain. The exact boundary defect F(r,x) has positive real-axis endpoint values. Any first interior contact must solve F=F_x=0, whose resultant is -r^16(r^6-4r^4+23r^2-9). The nontrivial factor is strictly increasing on (0,1), hence has one root rho. The linear subresultant gives a cosine in (-1,1), and the explicit canonical extremal reaches equality at that point. Convexity of the target parabolic domain upgrades the boundary inclusion to the full image domain.

value.rationale: The endpoint t=1/2 is the maximal univalent quadratic target in the fresh source, making its geometric radius a natural invariant rather than an arbitrary slice. The first obstruction is a nonreal tangency, so the sharp threshold is not obtained by a routine real-axis test. The exact algebraic radius and explicit extremal give a concrete benchmark for the newly introduced family and a base case for the full parameter-radius problem.
